title: Exceptional Topology Survives Strong Hermitian Fields in Radiative Atomic Arrays
authors: Tian-Shu Gou, Yi-Cheng Wang, Ya-Tang Yu, Guin-Dar Lin, Jhih-Shih You, H. H. Jen
abstract: Exceptional points are topological defects of complex band structures that are stable against weak perturbations, yet in bounded two-band systems they are ultimately removed by a sufficiently strong Hermitian field. Here we demonstrate a striking exception in a two-dimensional subwavelength atomic array. Along a continuous square-to-triangular deformation at fixed magnetic field, the bulk passes between line-gapped topological regions with band Chern numbers (C_1,C_2)=(2,-2) through a gapless exceptional region. Within a finite interval of lattice deformation, increasing the magnetic field merely drives the exceptional points toward the light cone because of the singular radiative dipolar couplings. We further show that skin localization toward open boundaries responds non-monotonically to the same field. An intermediate field drives a bipolar skin localization, with bulk modes accumulating at opposite edges, whereas stronger fields suppress boundary localization. Our results establish the interplay of lattice geometry, light-cone singularity, and Hermitian magnetic field as a route to engineering Chern and exceptional topology beyond the conventional strong-field limit.
summary: This paper analyzes the topological robustness of radiative atomic arrays by studying how exceptional points behave under strong magnetic fields. The authors show that the system's Chern topology remains fixed across various deformations, providing a method to engineer topological states beyond expected strong-field limitations. This work is significant for understanding topological control in engineered quantum optical systems.
main_problem: The study investigates how topological defects, specifically exceptional points (EPs), behave in two-dimensional subwavelength atomic arrays when subjected to strong Hermitian magnetic fields.
main_result: The research demonstrates that the topological invariants (Chern numbers) remain robust even when the system passes through exceptional regions, establishing a mechanism to engineer topology beyond conventional strong-field limits.
method: The authors employed analytical calculations of the Berry curvature and integrated Berry flux, alongside constructing effective models for phase boundaries near lattice deformation limits.
model_or_system: The system is a radiative atomic array modeled on a square-to-triangular lattice deformation, governed by a polarization-dependent Hamiltonian that includes radiative dipolar couplings.
key_observables: Berry Flux ($\pm 1$), Chern Numbers ($C_1=2, C_2=-2$), and the field-dependent localization of boundary modes (skin localization).
important_parameters: Lattice deformation angle ($	heta$), magnetic field strength ($B$), and the critical Zeeman shift ($\mu_B B_c$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximations such as first-order deformation expansions for boundary analysis and assuming decoupling from free-space modes for outer contributions.
figures_summary: Figure S8 illustrates the analytical exceptional-phase boundaries, mapping the critical Zeeman shift against lattice deformation for both the square and triangular lattice limits.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by deriving the Hamiltonian and calculating the Berry flux for the quadratic continuum model, followed by determining analytical phase boundaries for the SL and TL limits, and finally analyzing the non-monotonic response of skin localization to the magnetic field.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses topological phenomena in engineered quantum systems (atomic arrays) using concepts from condensed matter theory (Chern numbers, EPs) but is highly relevant to AMO physics due to the use of atomic lattices and light-matter interactions.
